Felder, `parked: Option<Parked>` und `unparked: Option<ParkRefusal>`; ein Struct-Literal außerhalb
des Crates muss sie also nennen, und in `--json` fehlen beide, solange sie nicht gesetzt sind.
`ParkOccasion` bekommt die Variante `PastItsBound` (`past_its_bound` in `--json` und an
`StatusOperation::park_refused.occasion`); das Enum ist `#[non_exhaustive]`, ein erschöpfendes
`match` außerhalb des Crates hatte also schon einen Auffangzweig.

items.en:
**`nxc withdraw` is a person's verb now: only whoever sent an operation's first commission may take
it back, and only by naming that thread.** Until now the bar was "may read the thread" — on a public
channel any handle, an agent's own `nxc` included — and `nxc prime` taught the verb to every session
that started. Since the verb can stop a running round, who may call it became the question, and the
answer is a person, or an assistant a person started. Three callers are now refused before anything
changes, each by name: **a session this workspace started** (`forbidden`) — whatever it names; the
refusal names the session and the role it was started for, and points it at `nxc reply --thread
<its own thread> --escalate -`, which goes up to whoever commissioned it; **a caller who did not
open the operation** (`forbidden`), told who did; and **a thread below the operation's first one** —
a step of a channel round, a sub-round an agent opened — (`validation`), told which thread to name
instead. The refusal of a session rests on what the engine can prove — the session map records
every session it started — and makes no claim beyond it: a process that hides its session is not
caught by that rule, and then meets the other two (nxf 6j6v.ezbr).

**`nxc prime` no longer offers the verb.** The `withdraw` line is gone from *How a conversation
moves*, the entry is gone from `--json`'s `commands` (seven entries now), and `when_stuck` points a
session with a held working copy at escalation instead. The shipped example team's `pm` persona says
the same.

**Facade contract.** `Engine::withdraw` / `orchestration::withdraw` refuse callers they used to
accept, which is why this is marked breaking although no signature moved: a `Caller` whose `session`
this workspace minted (`ErrorKind::Forbidden`), a caller that is not the opener of the thread's
operation (`Forbidden`; the read gate still answers first for a caller who cannot even read the
thread), and a thread that is not its operation's root (`Validation`). A host acting for its
logged-in user passes no session and withdraws what that user sent, exactly as before; a host that
withdrew a member thread it read off `status` now names the operation's root. `PRIME_COMMANDS` loses
its `withdraw` entry, and the texts of `PRIME_HOW_A_CONVERSATION_MOVES` and `PRIME_WHEN_STUCK`
changed accordingly.
items.de:
**`nxc withdraw` ist jetzt das Verb eines Menschen: Nur wer die erste Beauftragung eines Vorgangs
abgeschickt hat, darf sie zurücknehmen, und nur, indem er diesen Faden nennt.** Bisher lautete die
Hürde „darf den Faden lesen" — in einem öffentlichen Kanal jedes Handle, das eigene `nxc` eines
Agenten eingeschlossen —, und `nxc prime` brachte das Verb jeder startenden Sitzung bei. Seit das
Verb eine laufende Runde anhalten kann, ist die Frage, wer es aufrufen darf, und die Antwort ist ein
Mensch oder ein Assistent, den ein Mensch gestartet hat. Drei Aufrufer werden jetzt abgelehnt, bevor
sich etwas ändert, jeder benannt: **eine Sitzung, die dieser Workspace gestartet hat**
(`forbidden`) — gleich, was sie nennt; die Ablehnung nennt die Sitzung und die Rolle, für die sie
gestartet wurde, und verweist sie auf `nxc reply --thread <ihr eigener Faden> --escalate -`, das
nach oben geht, zu dem, der sie beauftragt hat; **wer den Vorgang nicht eröffnet hat**
(`forbidden`), mit dem Namen dessen, der es war; und **ein Faden unterhalb des ersten** — ein
Schritt einer Kanalrunde, eine Unterrunde, die ein Agent eröffnet hat — (`validation`), mit dem
Faden, der stattdessen zu nennen ist. Die Ablehnung einer Sitzung stützt sich auf das, was die
Engine belegen kann — die Sitzungstabelle verzeichnet jede Sitzung, die sie gestartet hat —, und
behauptet nicht mehr: Ein Prozess, der seine Sitzung verbirgt, fällt nicht unter diese Regel und
trifft dann auf die beiden anderen (nxf 6j6v.ezbr).

**`nxc prime` bietet das Verb nicht mehr an.** Die `withdraw`-Zeile ist aus *How a conversation
moves* verschwunden, der Eintrag aus `commands` in `--json` (jetzt sieben Einträge), und
`when_stuck` verweist eine Sitzung mit gehaltener Arbeitskopie stattdessen auf die Eskalation. Die
`pm`-Persona des mitgelieferten Beispielteams sagt dasselbe.

**Facade-Kontrakt.** `Engine::withdraw` / `orchestration::withdraw` lehnen Aufrufer ab, die sie
bisher angenommen haben — deshalb als breaking markiert, obwohl sich keine Signatur bewegt hat: ein
`Caller`, dessen `session` dieser Workspace erzeugt hat (`ErrorKind::Forbidden`), ein Aufrufer, der
nicht Eröffner des Vorgangs ist (`Forbidden`; wer den Faden nicht einmal lesen darf, bekommt weiter
zuerst die Ablehnung des Lese-Tors), und ein Faden, der nicht die Wurzel seines Vorgangs ist
(`Validation`). Ein Host, der für seinen angemeldeten Nutzer handelt, übergibt keine Sitzung und
nimmt zurück, was dieser Nutzer abgeschickt hat, genau wie bisher; ein Host, der einen aus `status`
gelesenen Mitglieds-Faden zurücknahm, nennt jetzt die Wurzel des Vorgangs. `PRIME_COMMANDS` verliert
den Eintrag `withdraw`, und die Texte von `PRIME_HOW_A_CONVERSATION_MOVES` und `PRIME_WHEN_STUCK`
haben sich entsprechend geändert.

items.en:
**`nxc withdraw` takes back a round that is already running, and parks its work.** Until now the
verb could only take back a commission that was still waiting for the working copy; a round whose
session had started was refused, and the only way to stop it was to find its process by hand — after
which nothing saved what it had left in the checkout, and the next holder started inside it. Now
`nxc withdraw --thread <id>` on a running round — by the person who sent it, see the entry on who
may withdraw — discharges the thread (the register says the round
is over), asks the chat worker to stop the session (the shipped sidecar receives `SIGTERM`, aborts
its turn, saves its transcript and announces its end), and — when the round holds this workspace's
working copy — records that its work is to be parked. The background tick then commits whatever the
session left uncommitted onto a branch once nothing in that operation is running any more, and hands
the copy on to whoever is waiting; with nobody waiting the copy simply becomes free. **Nothing is rolled back** at any point.
`nxc status` lists the branch under the operation until somebody comes back for it, and the way
back is the next commission into the same thread: on a direct persona thread, `nxc reply --thread
<id>` resumes the stopped session with its own transcript on the park branch; for a channel round, a
follow-up into the channel thread starts the next pass there. A fresh `send` opens a new claim and
does not find it (nxf 6j6v.b9nf).

**Between the stop and the park, the withdrawn holder keeps the copy.** The discharge leaves the
operation owing nothing, which is exactly the state the ordinary end-of-operation release fires on —
and a stopped session's own teardown or a late reply into the thread would have handed the copy on
with the work still in the tree. While the withdrawn marker stands, every such release declines;
the tick's withdrawn occasion is the one way such a holder lets go, and it acts only once nothing
in the claim area has a live process, re-checking once a minute while one still does. The refusal
rule applies unchanged: a park refused for a reason that can pass keeps the copy with `PARK
REFUSED` on `nxc status` and is retried; one that cannot pass hands the copy on unparked with the
named `work_handed_on_unparked` warning.

**A withdrawal interrupts the chain below the thread it names** (nxf 6j6v.s2cj). Every thread
between what was taken back and that thread that is still waiting — a channel thread owing its
round's result, a persona thread waiting on the round it commissioned — is discharged too, with a
message saying the chain was interrupted. So a channel commissions nothing further once one of its
steps is taken back: not the next step and not the taken-back step again, on a `flow: sequential`
channel and on one that declares `steps:` alike, before the park and after it; and nothing is
consolidated. The answers steps had already given stay in their threads, and the work comes back
when the person who withdrew it commissions the operation's first thread again — for a round an
agent commissioned, that thread's discharge carries the agent's session, so the follow-up resumes
it. (A round a withdrawal did not
discharge — one where a queued commission started while the withdrawal ran — is still held by the
marker: its settled set is not advanced, routed or consolidated until the copy has gone on.)

**What the receipt promises about a branch is now what the park can actually deliver.** `will_park`
used to mean only "this round holds the working copy", and said `true` on hosts where a park can
never succeed — a worker that names no working copy (the default of every worker but the shipped
sidecar), a workspace that is not a git repository, an operation with no recorded base. It now also
asks those three read-only preconditions, and when the round holds the copy but cannot be parked the
receipt carries `cannot_park` with the reason: the copy is still handed on once nothing in the
operation is running, unparked and with the `work_handed_on_unparked` warning saying so. `nxc
withdraw` prints that third case in its own words instead of "nothing of it is in this workspace's
working copy", and the message written into the withdrawn thread says the same true thing.

**And a withdrawal that leaves work for the tick says when there is nothing to run one.** While the
marker stands every other release path declines by design, so on a machine whose background service
is down the copy stays held by a round that is over, with nobody told. `nxc withdraw` now carries
the `service_not_running` warning `send`, `reply` and `tick` already carry (it does not change the
exit code), and both park lines name `nxc tick --thread <id>` — the command that does the park, or
the unparked hand-off, by hand.

**A host whose worker cannot stop a session is refused before anything changes** — the whole call,
by name (`this host cannot stop a running session; nothing was withdrawn`), so a withdrawal never
leaves a discharged thread beside a session that goes on writing. A stop the worker supports and
then could not deliver is a `session_not_stopped` warning on the receipt naming the session; the
thread is discharged all the same and the command exits non-zero. A session that had **already
ended** by the time the stop was sent — the ordinary race for a round that was about to finish — is
not a failure: the receipt carries a note saying what was found, `warnings` stays empty and the
command exits 0, because that is the state the call was asked for. And a host whose worker cannot
answer the liveness question at all is now refused **by name** — `ErrorKind::Validation`, where a
worker unable to answer liveness with an unended session in the area used to get `not_found` — when
the area holds sessions that never reported an end, instead of being told there is nothing to
withdraw: that answer was a statement about processes nobody had looked at. Apart from who may call
it and the chain it interrupts (both below and in the entry on who may withdraw), the queued case
behaves as before; the refusal for a thread with nothing under it (a worker that DOES answer
liveness, or an area with no unended session either way) is still `not_found` and now reads
*nothing under thread … is waiting or running*.

**And a withdrawn holder that will not leave now has a visible reason.** A stopped session can
survive its `SIGTERM` — a wedged sidecar, a custom worker whose stop returns `Ok` and changes
nothing, a reused pid — and until now nothing on any surface said so: `nxc status` had no field for
it, and "stop it by hand" printed only when the very first `stop_session` call had itself errored,
never when the request landed and was simply ignored. `nxc status` now marks the holding operation
`WITHDRAWN` (beside `PARK REFUSED` and `holds working tree`) and names who withdrew it, when, and
every session still pinning the claim right now; `--json` carries the same fact as a new
`withdrawn` field, omitted when the operation's round was never withdrawn. And after five liveness
cadences (five minutes) with a session the withdrawal stopped still there, `nxc tick` sends it **one
further `SIGTERM`** — through the worker's own stop, behind the same identity check as the first —
and names it: the session, its pid, the pid file that names it, and when that further signal went
(nxf 6j6v.27b9). Nothing more is ever sent, and never `SIGKILL`: the sidecar's whole teardown
happens on `SIGTERM`, and ending the process past that is left to a person. Against the shipped
sidecar, which is already stopping when it arrives, that further signal changes nothing; it helps a
host's own worker whose first stop was lost or ignored. A session a follow-up put back in motion
before the park is somebody's work again, and is neither signalled nor named.

**Facade contract.** `WithdrawReceipt` gains `stopped: Vec<StoppedSession>` (`{thread, role,
session, already_gone?}` — the last omitted unless the session had already ended, in which case it
carries the sentence saying so; the array omitted from `--json` when empty), `will_park: bool`,
`cannot_park: Option<String>` (omitted from `--json` when absent; `will_park: false` with no
`cannot_park` is a round that holds nothing, `cannot_park: Some(_)` is work in the checkout this
host can never park) and `warnings: Vec<FailedConsequence>` (omitted when empty), and is now
`#[non_exhaustive]` — both the new fields
and the marker break a struct literal written outside the crate, which is why this is marked
breaking; reading the receipt is unaffected. `ParkOccasion` gains `Withdrawn` (`withdrawn` in
`--json` and on `park_refused.occasion`); `ConsequenceClass` gains `SessionNotStopped`
(`session_not_stopped`) and `WithdrawnHolderWedged` (`withdrawn_holder_wedged`); both enums were
already `#[non_exhaustive]`. `ChatStore` gains `note_withdrawn_holder`, `withdrawn_holder` and
`all_withdrawn_holders` over the new device-local table `withdrawn_holders`, and
`note_withdrawn_sessions`, `withdrawn_session` (a new `WithdrawnSession {stopped_at, resignalled_at,
resignal_refused}`), `claim_withdrawn_session_resignal`, `note_withdrawn_session_resignal_refused`
and `forget_withdrawn_session` over its sibling `withdrawn_sessions` — the sessions a withdrawal
stopped, which are the only ones the tick's further `SIGTERM` may reach.
`StatusOperation` — also `#[non_exhaustive]` already — gains `withdrawn: Option<WithdrawnHolderStatus>`
(the new type, `#[non_exhaustive]`: `{withdrawn_at, by, pinned_by: Vec<String>}`), a purely
additive field. `Engine::withdraw`'s signature is unchanged.
items.de:
**`nxc withdraw` nimmt eine bereits laufende Runde zurück und parkt ihre Arbeit.** Bisher konnte das
Verb nur eine Beauftragung zurücknehmen, die noch auf die Arbeitskopie wartete; eine Runde, deren
Sitzung gestartet war, wurde abgelehnt, und der einzige Weg, sie anzuhalten, war, ihren Prozess von
Hand zu suchen — wonach nichts sicherte, was sie in der Arbeitskopie hinterlassen hatte, und der
nächste Halter darin startete. Jetzt entlastet `nxc withdraw --thread <id>` auf einer laufenden
Runde — durch den Menschen, der sie abgeschickt hat, siehe den Eintrag dazu, wer zurücknehmen darf —
den Faden (das Register sagt, die Runde ist vorbei), bittet den Chat-Worker, die Sitzung
anzuhalten (der mitgelieferte Sidecar erhält `SIGTERM`, bricht seinen Zug ab, sichert sein
Transkript und meldet sein Ende), und vermerkt — wenn die Runde die Arbeitskopie dieses Workspace
hält —, dass ihre Arbeit zu parken ist. Der Hintergrund-Tick committet dann, sobald in diesem
Vorgang nichts mehr läuft, alles Uncommittete auf einen Zweig und gibt die Kopie an den weiter, der
wartet; wartet niemand, wird die Kopie einfach frei. **Nichts wird je zurückgerollt.** `nxc status` führt den Zweig
unter dem Vorgang, bis jemand ihn wieder abholt, und der Weg zurück ist die nächste Beauftragung in
denselben Faden: auf einem direkten Persona-Faden setzt `nxc reply --thread <id>` die angehaltene
Sitzung mit ihrem eigenen Transkript auf dem Parkzweig fort; bei einer Kanalrunde startet eine
Folgenachricht in den Kanalfaden dort den nächsten Durchgang. Ein frisches `send` eröffnet einen
neuen Anspruch und findet sie nicht (nxf 6j6v.b9nf).

**Zwischen Stopp und Parken behält der zurückgenommene Halter die Kopie.** Die Entlastung lässt den
Vorgang nichts mehr schulden — genau der Zustand, in dem die gewöhnliche Freigabe am Ende eines
Vorgangs greift —, und der Abbau der angehaltenen Sitzung oder eine späte Antwort in den Faden hätte
die Kopie mit der Arbeit noch im Baum weitergegeben. Solange die Markierung steht, unterbleibt jede
solche Freigabe; der Anlass „zurückgenommen" des Ticks ist der eine Weg, auf dem ein solcher Halter
loslässt, und er handelt erst, wenn nichts im Anspruchsbereich mehr einen lebenden Prozess hat —
solange einer da ist, sieht er einmal pro Minute nach. Die Ablehnungsregel gilt unverändert: Ein
Parken, das aus einem behebbaren Grund abgelehnt wird, behält die Kopie mit `PARK REFUSED` in
`nxc status` und wird erneut versucht; eines, das nie durchgehen kann, gibt die Kopie ungeparkt mit
der benannten Warnung `work_handed_on_unparked` weiter.

**Eine Rücknahme unterbricht die Kette unter dem Faden, den sie nennt** (nxf 6j6v.s2cj). Jeder
Faden zwischen dem Zurückgenommenen und diesem Faden, der noch wartet — ein Kanalfaden, der das
Ergebnis seiner Runde schuldet, ein Persona-Faden, der auf die von ihm beauftragte Runde wartet —,
wird ebenfalls entlastet, mit einer Nachricht, die sagt, dass die Kette unterbrochen wurde. Ein
Kanal beauftragt also nichts mehr, sobald einer seiner Schritte zurückgenommen ist: weder den
nächsten Schritt noch den zurückgenommenen erneut, an einem `flow: sequential`-Kanal genauso wie an
einem mit `steps:`, vor dem Parken und danach; und nichts wird zusammengeführt. Die Antworten, die
Schritte schon gegeben hatten, bleiben in ihren Fäden, und die Arbeit kommt zurück, wenn der Mensch,
der sie zurückgenommen hat, den ersten Faden des Vorgangs erneut beauftragt — bei einer Runde, die
ein Agent beauftragt hat, trägt die Entlastung dieses Fadens die Sitzung des Agenten, sodass die
Folgenachricht sie fortsetzt. (Eine Runde, die eine Rücknahme nicht
entlastet hat — eine, in der eine wartende Beauftragung startete, während die Rücknahme lief —, hält
weiter die Markierung: Ihr abgeschlossener Satz wird weder fortgeschaltet noch geroutet noch
zusammengeführt, bis die Kopie weitergegeben ist.)

**Was die Quittung über einen Zweig verspricht, ist jetzt das, was das Parken auch liefern kann.**
`will_park` hieß bisher nur „diese Runde hält die Arbeitskopie" und stand auf `true` auch auf Hosts,
auf denen ein Parken nie gelingen kann — ein Worker, der keine Arbeitskopie benennt (die Vorgabe
jedes Workers außer dem mitgelieferten Sidecar), ein Workspace, der kein Git-Repository ist, ein
Vorgang ohne vermerkte Basis. Jetzt werden diese drei rein lesenden Vorbedingungen mitgefragt, und
wenn die Runde die Kopie zwar hält, aber nicht geparkt werden kann, trägt die Quittung
`cannot_park` mit dem Grund: Die Kopie wird trotzdem weitergegeben, sobald im Vorgang nichts mehr
läuft — ungeparkt und mit der Warnung `work_handed_on_unparked`, die das sagt. `nxc withdraw` gibt
diesen dritten Fall in eigenen Worten aus statt „nothing of it is in this workspace's working copy",
und die in den zurückgenommenen Faden geschriebene Nachricht sagt dasselbe Wahre.

**Und eine Rücknahme, die dem Tick Arbeit hinterlässt, sagt, wenn nichts einen Tick ausführt.**
Solange die Markierung steht, unterbleibt jede andere Freigabe planmäßig — auf einer Maschine mit
totem Hintergrunddienst bleibt die Kopie also bei einer Runde, die vorbei ist, ohne dass es jemand
erfährt. `nxc withdraw` trägt jetzt die Warnung `service_not_running`, die `send`, `reply` und
`tick` schon tragen (sie ändert den Exit-Code nicht), und beide Park-Zeilen nennen
`nxc tick --thread <id>` — den Befehl, der das Parken beziehungsweise die ungeparkte Weitergabe von
Hand erledigt.

**Ein Host, dessen Worker keine Sitzung anhalten kann, wird abgelehnt, bevor sich etwas ändert** —
der ganze Aufruf, benannt (`this host cannot stop a running session; nothing was withdrawn`), damit
eine Rücknahme nie einen entlasteten Faden neben einer weiterschreibenden Sitzung hinterlässt. Ein
Stopp, den der Worker beherrscht und dann nicht zustellen konnte, ist eine Warnung
`session_not_stopped` auf der Quittung, die die Sitzung nennt; der Faden ist trotzdem entlastet, und
der Befehl endet mit einem Fehlercode. Eine Sitzung, die zum Zeitpunkt des Stopps **bereits beendet**
war — das gewöhnliche Rennen bei einer Runde, die ohnehin gerade fertig wurde —, ist kein
Fehlschlag: Die Quittung trägt einen Vermerk, was vorgefunden wurde, `warnings` bleibt leer, und der
Befehl endet mit 0, denn das ist genau der Zustand, um den es ging. Und ein Host, dessen Worker die
Lebendigkeitsfrage überhaupt nicht beantworten kann, wird jetzt **benannt** abgelehnt —
`ErrorKind::Validation`, wo ein Worker, der die Lebendigkeit nicht beantworten kann, bei einer nicht
gemeldeten Sitzung im Bereich bisher `not_found` bekam —, wenn im Bereich Sitzungen ohne gemeldetes
Ende liegen, statt zu hören, es gebe nichts zurückzunehmen: Diese Antwort war eine Aussage über
Prozesse, die niemand angesehen hatte. Abgesehen davon, wer zurücknehmen darf, und von der Kette,
die eine Rücknahme unterbricht (beides unten und im Eintrag dazu, wer zurücknehmen darf), verhält
sich der wartende Fall wie bisher; die Ablehnung für einen Faden, unter dem nichts liegt (ein
Worker, der die Lebendigkeit beantworten kann, oder ein Bereich ganz ohne nicht gemeldete Sitzung),
bleibt `not_found` und lautet jetzt *nothing under thread … is waiting or running*.

**Und ein Halter, der die Rücknahme nicht loslässt, hat jetzt einen sichtbaren Grund.** Eine
angehaltene Sitzung kann ihr `SIGTERM` überleben — ein hängender Sidecar, ein eigener Worker, dessen
Stopp `Ok` meldet und nichts ändert, eine wiederverwendete PID —, und bisher sagte das nichts auf
keiner Oberfläche: `nxc status` hatte dafür kein Feld, und „von Hand stoppen" stand nur dann, wenn
schon der erste `stop_session`-Aufruf selbst fehlgeschlagen war, nie wenn die Anforderung ankam und
einfach ignoriert wurde. `nxc status` markiert den haltenden Vorgang jetzt mit `WITHDRAWN` (neben
`PARK REFUSED` und `holds working tree`) und nennt, wer zurückgenommen hat, wann, und jede Sitzung,
die den Anspruch gerade noch hält; `--json` trägt dieselbe Tatsache als neues Feld `withdrawn`,
weggelassen, wenn die Runde des Vorgangs nie zurückgenommen wurde. Und nach fünf
Lebendigkeits-Takten (fünf Minuten), in denen eine von der Rücknahme gestoppte Sitzung noch da ist,
schickt `nxc tick` ihr **ein weiteres `SIGTERM`** — über den eigenen Stopp des Workers, hinter
derselben Identitätsprüfung wie das erste — und nennt sie: die Sitzung, ihre PID, die PID-Datei, die
sie nennt, und wann dieses weitere Signal ging (nxf 6j6v.27b9). Mehr wird nie geschickt, und nie
`SIGKILL`: Der ganze Abbau des Sidecars geschieht auf `SIGTERM`, und den Prozess darüber hinaus zu
beenden, bleibt einem Menschen überlassen. Beim mitgelieferten Sidecar, der beim Eintreffen schon
anhält, ändert dieses weitere Signal nichts; es hilft dem eigenen Worker eines Hosts, dessen erster
Stopp verloren ging oder ignoriert wurde. Eine Sitzung, die eine Folgenachricht vor dem Parken
wieder in Gang gesetzt hat, ist wieder jemandes Arbeit und wird weder signalisiert noch genannt.

**Facade-Kontrakt.** `WithdrawReceipt` bekommt `stopped: Vec<StoppedSession>` (`{thread, role,
session, already_gone?}` — das letzte Feld nur, wenn die Sitzung bereits beendet war, dann mit dem
Satz, der das sagt; das Array in `--json` weggelassen, wenn leer), `will_park: bool`,
`cannot_park: Option<String>` (in `--json` weggelassen, wenn nicht gesetzt; `will_park: false` ohne
`cannot_park` ist eine Runde, die nichts hält, `cannot_park: Some(_)` ist Arbeit in der
Arbeitskopie, die dieser Host nie parken kann) und `warnings: Vec<FailedConsequence>` (weggelassen,
wenn leer) und ist jetzt `#[non_exhaustive]` — sowohl die
neuen Felder als auch die Markierung brechen ein außerhalb des Crates geschriebenes Struct-Literal,
weshalb dies als breaking markiert ist; das Lesen der Quittung ist nicht betroffen. `ParkOccasion`
bekommt `Withdrawn` (`withdrawn` in `--json` und an `park_refused.occasion`); `ConsequenceClass`
bekommt `SessionNotStopped` (`session_not_stopped`) und `WithdrawnHolderWedged`
(`withdrawn_holder_wedged`); beide Enums waren bereits `#[non_exhaustive]`.
`ChatStore` bekommt `note_withdrawn_holder`, `withdrawn_holder` und `all_withdrawn_holders` über die
neue gerätelokale Tabelle `withdrawn_holders`, und `note_withdrawn_sessions`, `withdrawn_session`
(ein neues `WithdrawnSession {stopped_at, resignalled_at, resignal_refused}`),
`claim_withdrawn_session_resignal`, `note_withdrawn_session_resignal_refused` und
`forget_withdrawn_session` über ihre Schwester `withdrawn_sessions` — die Sitzungen, die eine
Rücknahme gestoppt hat, und damit die einzigen, die das weitere `SIGTERM` des Ticks erreichen darf. `StatusOperation` — ebenfalls schon
`#[non_exhaustive]` — bekommt `withdrawn: Option<WithdrawnHolderStatus>` (der neue Typ, auch
`#[non_exhaustive]`: `{withdrawn_at, by, pinned_by: Vec<String>}`), ein rein additives Feld. Die
Signatur von `Engine::withdraw` ist unverändert.

notes.en:
### Added
- **A chat worker can now stop a session it started.** Until now the engine could only ask a worker
questions about a session — is it running, where does it run, can it be resumed — and the one thing
that ended a session was the session itself. That is the piece a withdrawal of a *running* round
needs and did not have: taking the work back while its session goes on writing into the checkout
leaves the park stale before its receipt is printed. The shipped sidecar worker answers the new
question with yes and stops a session by sending its process `SIGTERM` — never `SIGKILL`, never the
whole process group — to the pid recorded in the same `.nxs/agent-logs/<session>.pid` file the
liveness check reads, so the process signalled is by construction the one reported as running. A
missing pid file, a file that holds no pid, or a claim that cannot prove which process it names is
refused by name rather than signalled into the dark; a session whose process is already gone is not
a failure at all but the state the stop was asked for, reported as such. The request is *delivered*,
not waited out: whoever stops a session watches the liveness check turn false before touching the
tree (nxf 6j6v.b9nf).

**A session claim now records WHICH process holds it, not only its number.** Claims are deliberately
never removed, so a session that crashed — or a machine that rebooted — leaves a file naming a pid
the operating system is free to hand to something else: an editor, a dev server, another `nxc` of
the same user. `kill(pid, 0)` says *yes* about that stranger, which was tolerable while the answer
only delayed a wake and is not tolerable now that taking a round back sends the process a signal. So
`.nxs/agent-logs/<session>.pid` holds the pid on its first line and the instant that process started
on its second, and every reader compares that instant against what the operating system reports for
the pid it finds — the same identity check the background service already makes for its own
heartbeat, shared rather than copied. A claim whose instant disagrees names a session that **ended**:
it reads as not running, and nothing is signalled. A claim written before this existed records no
instant, cannot be told apart from a recycled pid, and is therefore refused by name instead of
signalled — the liveness reads still believe it, because being wrong there costs a delayed turn
while being wrong about a signal costs a stranger's process.

**And the liveness checks now read a pid file the same way the stop does.** A `.pid` file holding
`0` — or any number the operating system would read as a process *group* rather than a process —
reads as *no live process* everywhere: for one session, and for the whole-workspace list the
background service polls. Both used to parse a bare number and ask `kill(pid, 0)` about it, which
for `0` is a question about the asking process's own group and answers *yes* whenever anything of
this workspace is alive — a session reported as running that nothing could ever end.

**The sidecar tears down on `SIGTERM` instead of dying.** It aborts the running turn through the
SDK's own abort door, then runs its teardown in the usual order — binds the runtime session so a
later resume can find the conversation, flushes everything the aborted turn produced into the
transcript, and announces `nxc session ended`. Exactly one step is skipped on the signal: the
session is **not reminded** to answer, because a reminder tells a session it broke the answering
rule and this one was told to stop, and it would spend a model call doing so.

**Whether anything is posted in the session's name is decided by the BOARD, not by the signal.** A
`SIGTERM` is not only a withdrawal: it is a system shutdown, a logout, a `docker stop`, a person's
`kill <pid>`. A withdrawal discharges the thread before it signals, so the teardown reads a thread
that owes nothing and says nothing — which is right, because a substitute reply there would speak
as the agent into a round that has just been taken back. Every other `SIGTERM` leaves the thread
still owing an answer, and the teardown posts the usual `nxc reply --thread <id> --if-unanswered`
for it; the engine's own gate still decides whether that write lands. Without this the handler
turned every outside `SIGTERM` from a hard death — which the dead-holder sweep frees in about a
minute — into a tidy silent end, because the teardown now announces the session's end: the debt
unsettled, the waiting caller unwoken, and the working copy held until the two-hour bound.

A stop is neither a finished turn nor a failed one, so the log ends in `sidecar stopped:` rather
than `sidecar done:`, and the process exits with **143** (128 + SIGTERM, the number a shell reports
for a process that died of the signal, kept for one that caught it). A `SIGTERM` that arrives during
the reply-reminder round ends that round the same way.

**Facade contract.** `Worker` gains two defaulted methods: `stops_sessions(&self) -> bool`
(`false` by default — a host that cannot stop a session is refused by name rather than believed)
and `stop_session(&self, internal_session: &str) -> Result<SessionStop, String>` (a named refusal by
default). An existing implementation keeps exactly the behaviour it had; a host whose runtime can
stop its own sessions overrides both. `WorkerConfig::Custom`'s wrapper forwards both. The new
`SessionStop` enum (`#[non_exhaustive]`) is what a delivered stop and an already-finished session
are told apart by: `Requested` is the signal sent, `NothingToStop(String)` is the goal state with the
sentence that found it — a caller puts that on its receipt rather than in a warning. `worker` also
gains `session_claim_for(pid) -> String`, the one spelling of a claim file's contents, so anything
standing a process in for a session writes the shape the readers expect. Nothing was removed.
- **`nxc status` now names an operation's unresumed parked work.** Since nxf 6j6v.de9s a stranded
escalation could be parked onto a branch and the working copy handed on — but the only way to find
that branch again was to already know it existed. Now the operation's own line on `nxc status`
carries one line per unresumed park: the branch, the commit's first seven characters, and when the
copy was handed on (plus a note when the park found nothing to commit). `--json` carries the same
rows as `parked` on the operation, and a workspace that has never parked stays silent about the
field — no `"parked"` key at all.

For embedding apps: `StatusOperation` (from `Engine::status`) gains a `parked` field. It was
already `#[non_exhaustive]`, so nothing changes for a reader.
- **`nxc withdraw` takes back a round that is already running, and parks its work.** Until now the
verb could only take back a commission that was still waiting for the working copy; a round whose
session had started was refused, and the only way to stop it was to find its process by hand — after
which nothing saved what it had left in the checkout, and the next holder started inside it. Now
`nxc withdraw --thread <id>` on a running round — by the person who sent it, see the entry on who
may withdraw — discharges the thread (the register says the round
is over), asks the chat worker to stop the session (the shipped sidecar receives `SIGTERM`, aborts
its turn, saves its transcript and announces its end), and — when the round holds this workspace's
working copy — records that its work is to be parked. The background tick then commits whatever the
session left uncommitted onto a branch once nothing in that operation is running any more, and hands
the copy on to whoever is waiting; with nobody waiting the copy simply becomes free. **Nothing is rolled back** at any point.
`nxc status` lists the branch under the operation until somebody comes back for it, and the way
back is the next commission into the same thread: on a direct persona thread, `nxc reply --thread
<id>` resumes the stopped session with its own transcript on the park branch; for a channel round, a
follow-up into the channel thread starts the next pass there. A fresh `send` opens a new claim and
does not find it (nxf 6j6v.b9nf).

**Between the stop and the park, the withdrawn holder keeps the copy.** The discharge leaves the
operation owing nothing, which is exactly the state the ordinary end-of-operation release fires on —
and a stopped session's own teardown or a late reply into the thread would have handed the copy on
with the work still in the tree. While the withdrawn marker stands, every such release declines;
the tick's withdrawn occasion is the one way such a holder lets go, and it acts only once nothing
in the claim area has a live process, re-checking once a minute while one still does. The refusal
rule applies unchanged: a park refused for a reason that can pass keeps the copy with `PARK
REFUSED` on `nxc status` and is retried; one that cannot pass hands the copy on unparked with the
named `work_handed_on_unparked` warning.

**A withdrawal interrupts the chain below the thread it names** (nxf 6j6v.s2cj). Every thread
between what was taken back and that thread that is still waiting — a channel thread owing its
round's result, a persona thread waiting on the round it commissioned — is discharged too, with a
message saying the chain was interrupted. So a channel commissions nothing further once one of its
steps is taken back: not the next step and not the taken-back step again, on a `flow: sequential`
channel and on one that declares `steps:` alike, before the park and after it; and nothing is
consolidated. The answers steps had already given stay in their threads, and the work comes back
when the person who withdrew it commissions the operation's first thread again — for a round an
agent commissioned, that thread's discharge carries the agent's session, so the follow-up resumes
it. (A round a withdrawal did not
discharge — one where a queued commission started while the withdrawal ran — is still held by the
marker: its settled set is not advanced, routed or consolidated until the copy has gone on.)

**What the receipt promises about a branch is now what the park can actually deliver.** `will_park`
used to mean only "this round holds the working copy", and said `true` on hosts where a park can
never succeed — a worker that names no working copy (the default of every worker but the shipped
sidecar), a workspace that is not a git repository, an operation with no recorded base. It now also
asks those three read-only preconditions, and when the round holds the copy but cannot be parked the
receipt carries `cannot_park` with the reason: the copy is still handed on once nothing in the
operation is running, unparked and with the `work_handed_on_unparked` warning saying so. `nxc
withdraw` prints that third case in its own words instead of "nothing of it is in this workspace's
working copy", and the message written into the withdrawn thread says the same true thing.

**And a withdrawal that leaves work for the tick says when there is nothing to run one.** While the
marker stands every other release path declines by design, so on a machine whose background service
is down the copy stays held by a round that is over, with nobody told. `nxc withdraw` now carries
the `service_not_running` warning `send`, `reply` and `tick` already carry (it does not change the
exit code), and both park lines name `nxc tick --thread <id>` — the command that does the park, or
the unparked hand-off, by hand.

**A host whose worker cannot stop a session is refused before anything changes** — the whole call,
by name (`this host cannot stop a running session; nothing was withdrawn`), so a withdrawal never
leaves a discharged thread beside a session that goes on writing. A stop the worker supports and
then could not deliver is a `session_not_stopped` warning on the receipt naming the session; the
thread is discharged all the same and the command exits non-zero. A session that had **already
ended** by the time the stop was sent — the ordinary race for a round that was about to finish — is
not a failure: the receipt carries a note saying what was found, `warnings` stays empty and the
command exits 0, because that is the state the call was asked for. And a host whose worker cannot
answer the liveness question at all is now refused **by name** — `ErrorKind::Validation`, where a
worker unable to answer liveness with an unended session in the area used to get `not_found` — when
the area holds sessions that never reported an end, instead of being told there is nothing to
withdraw: that answer was a statement about processes nobody had looked at. Apart from who may call
it and the chain it interrupts (both below and in the entry on who may withdraw), the queued case
behaves as before; the refusal for a thread with nothing under it (a worker that DOES answer
liveness, or an area with no unended session either way) is still `not_found` and now reads
*nothing under thread … is waiting or running*.

**And a withdrawn holder that will not leave now has a visible reason.** A stopped session can
survive its `SIGTERM` — a wedged sidecar, a custom worker whose stop returns `Ok` and changes
nothing, a reused pid — and until now nothing on any surface said so: `nxc status` had no field for
it, and "stop it by hand" printed only when the very first `stop_session` call had itself errored,
never when the request landed and was simply ignored. `nxc status` now marks the holding operation
`WITHDRAWN` (beside `PARK REFUSED` and `holds working tree`) and names who withdrew it, when, and
every session still pinning the claim right now; `--json` carries the same fact as a new
`withdrawn` field, omitted when the operation's round was never withdrawn. And after five liveness
cadences (five minutes) with a session the withdrawal stopped still there, `nxc tick` sends it **one
further `SIGTERM`** — through the worker's own stop, behind the same identity check as the first —
and names it: the session, its pid, the pid file that names it, and when that further signal went
(nxf 6j6v.27b9). Nothing more is ever sent, and never `SIGKILL`: the sidecar's whole teardown
happens on `SIGTERM`, and ending the process past that is left to a person. Against the shipped
sidecar, which is already stopping when it arrives, that further signal changes nothing; it helps a
host's own worker whose first stop was lost or ignored. A session a follow-up put back in motion
before the park is somebody's work again, and is neither signalled nor named.

**Facade contract.** `WithdrawReceipt` gains `stopped: Vec<StoppedSession>` (`{thread, role,
session, already_gone?}` — the last omitted unless the session had already ended, in which case it
carries the sentence saying so; the array omitted from `--json` when empty), `will_park: bool`,
`cannot_park: Option<String>` (omitted from `--json` when absent; `will_park: false` with no
`cannot_park` is a round that holds nothing, `cannot_park: Some(_)` is work in the checkout this
host can never park) and `warnings: Vec<FailedConsequence>` (omitted when empty), and is now
`#[non_exhaustive]` — both the new fields
and the marker break a struct literal written outside the crate, which is why this is marked
breaking; reading the receipt is unaffected. `ParkOccasion` gains `Withdrawn` (`withdrawn` in
`--json` and on `park_refused.occasion`); `ConsequenceClass` gains `SessionNotStopped`
(`session_not_stopped`) and `WithdrawnHolderWedged` (`withdrawn_holder_wedged`); both enums were
already `#[non_exhaustive]`. `ChatStore` gains `note_withdrawn_holder`, `withdrawn_holder` and
`all_withdrawn_holders` over the new device-local table `withdrawn_holders`, and
`note_withdrawn_sessions`, `withdrawn_session` (a new `WithdrawnSession {stopped_at, resignalled_at,
resignal_refused}`), `claim_withdrawn_session_resignal`, `note_withdrawn_session_resignal_refused`
and `forget_withdrawn_session` over its sibling `withdrawn_sessions` — the sessions a withdrawal
stopped, which are the only ones the tick's further `SIGTERM` may reach.

### Changed

escalation or an operation on hold at an availability boundary has to give up the working copy, its
work is parked first — and a park can be refused. Until now every refusal kept the checkout where it
was and named `nxc release` as the way out. Owner decision of 2026-09-17 (nxf 6j6v.8bv9,
6j6v.b9nf): a refusal that can pass (a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert or bisect in progress, or a
git command that failed) keeps the checkout, is reported as `work_not_parked` with what to finish,
shows on `nxc status` as `PARK REFUSED` with a line `park refused (<refusal>): <detail> — retrying
since <instant>`, and is retried by the background service on every tick — and only for as long as
the trouble that wanted the checkout lasts: once the escalation is answered, the operation on hold is
taken up, or nobody is waiting any more, the mark goes on the next tick, because nothing is retrying
that park then. A refusal that cannot pass (the runtime names no working copy, the directory is not a
git repository, no base branch was ever recorded) hands the checkout on WITHOUT parking and says so
as the new `work_handed_on_unparked` warning — the operation's uncommitted files stay in the tree for
the next holder. An operation on hold at an availability boundary is now also secured by the tick
while somebody waits, not only by `nxc resume`. No refusal text names `nxc release` any more. And an
operation with unresumed parked work or a refused park now stays on the default `nxc status` listing
even when nothing else about it is open.

crate has to name it. `ConsequenceClass` gains `WorkHandedOnUnparked` (already `#[non_exhaustive]`).

`#[non_exhaustive]`), and `ChatStore` gains `note_park_refusal`, `clear_park_refusal`,

`occasion` that refused the park (`stranded_escalation`, `availability_boundary`), in `--json` too.

working copy on for a host whose worker names no working copy (the default of every worker but the
sidecar) where they used to leave it held.

(nxf), the memory (nxm) and the channel (nxc) your agents work from, in one binary" instead of "nxs
platform umbrella CLI", and the `nxs init` welcome box opens with the README's tagline. The welcome

removes. When HEAD is on the operation's recorded base branch and the tree is clean, the park now

instead. The refusal of a session rests on what the engine can prove — the session map records
every session it started — and makes no claim beyond it: a process that hides its session is not
caught by that rule, and then meets the other two (nxf 6j6v.ezbr).

moves*, the entry is gone from `--json`'s `commands` (seven entries now), and `when_stuck` points a
session with a held working copy at escalation instead. The shipped example team's `pm` persona says
the same.

changed accordingly.

### Fixed
- **A commission no longer waits out two hours behind an operation that is already dead.** The
working-tree lease has a two-hour backstop, and until now that backstop was the only thing watching:
if the chain holding the checkout died hard — crashed, killed, machine asleep — nothing released it,
nothing looked, and whoever was queued behind it stood still until the lease expired. Now the
background tick asks, once a minute while anybody is waiting, whether the holder is *provably* gone,
and takes the checkout as soon as it is: the dead operation's work is committed to a branch
(untracked files included; anything your `.gitignore` excludes stays in the tree), the tree goes back
to the branch that operation started on, and the waiting commission starts — typically within a
minute of the death instead of up to two hours later (nxf 6j6v.xb24).

**"Provably" is five conditions, and all five have to hold**, because taking a checkout away writes
into it. The chat worker must actually be able to answer the process question — a runtime that cannot
look never takes a checkout early, so nothing changes for a host that does not implement the liveness
probe. At least one thread of that operation must still owe an answer; an operation whose sessions
all ended normally and handed the task back is not dead but waiting for a human, and it keeps the
thirty-minute contention rule it already had. Nothing in the operation may have a live process. No
owing thread's session may have reported its end — a reported end is a teardown that ran, which is
not a hard death. And nothing in the operation may be on hold at an availability boundary, which has
its own path and its own way back. What that check costs was measured before it was put in every
tick, and measured end to end: about **two milliseconds** for an operation of twenty threads with
twenty sessions, on a development machine, in the slower of the two builds this project makes.

Everything else about this hand-off is the behaviour the other occasions already had: `nxc tick`
reports where the work went, `nxc status` shows the parked branch on the operation until it is
resumed, and the refusal rule applies unchanged — a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert or bisect in
progress, or a git command that failed, **keeps the checkout** with the operation marked
`PARK REFUSED` and the park retried every tick, while a refusal that can never pass (no working copy,
not a git repository, no base branch ever recorded) hands the checkout on unparked with the named
`work_handed_on_unparked` warning.

**One timing change you may notice.** While a commission is queued behind a claim, the tick that
re-checks it is now scheduled a minute out rather than at the holder's own bound — that re-check is
what makes the above arrive in a minute instead of at the bound. A bound that falls sooner than a
minute still wins; nothing is ever pushed later.

**Facade contract.** `ParkOccasion` gains the variant `DiedInsideItsBound`
(`died_inside_its_bound` in `--json` and on `StatusOperation::park_refused.occasion`), and
`TickReceipt::handed_on` can now carry it; the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so an exhaustive `match`
outside the crate already had a wildcard. `ChatStore` gains
`reclaim_a_dead_holders_working_tree_and_take_next`, the compare-and-swap twin of
`reclaim_expired_working_tree_and_take_next` for a lease that is still inside its bound. Nothing was
removed and no signature changed.
- **A tick no longer consolidates a withdrawn round and wakes the agent that commissioned it.** When
every commission of a channel round was taken back, the channel thread was discharged as withdrawn —
and the channel's own clock could still fire on it later, read a settled set, and deliver it: for a
round a person had commissioned that was a no-op, but for one an agent had commissioned (a `pm`
that sent work to a channel) it woke that agent with the taken-back round as its answer, and the
work went on. `nxc tick` now treats a thread discharged by a withdrawal as already handled, exactly
like one that was consolidated (`reason: already_handled`), and nothing is delivered (nxf
6j6v.s2cj).
- **A holder that dies without saying anything no longer loses its uncommitted work when the queue
takes its checkout.** When a working-tree lease runs out and nothing in that operation's chain still
has a live process, the background sweep hands the checkout to whoever is waiting — and until now it
did that with the dead operation's uncommitted files still in the tree, so the next agent started
inside somebody else's half-finished work. It was the last hand-off caused by trouble that saved
nothing first: a chain that crashed never escalated and never announced an availability boundary, so
neither of the two parks that already existed was ever asked about it (nxf 6j6v.8bv9). Now its work
is committed to a branch (untracked files included; anything your `.gitignore` excludes stays in the
tree), the checkout goes back to the branch that operation started on, and only then does the waiting
commission start — `nxc tick` reports the park on the same block as the reclaim, and `nxc status`
shows the parked branch on the operation until it is resumed. The refusal rule applies here exactly
as it does to the other two occasions: a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert or bisect in progress, or
a git command that failed, now **keeps the checkout** with the operation marked `PARK REFUSED` and
the park retried on every tick — where before the same tick said the claim was staying and then
reclaimed it two steps later, which is the one contradiction this release removes. A refusal that
cannot pass (no working copy, not a git repository, no base branch ever recorded) hands the checkout
on unparked with the named `work_handed_on_unparked` warning, as it already did elsewhere. A holder
that is past its bound but still has a live process is untouched, exactly as before.

**The same is now true of the other door onto that moment.** A newcomer's own `nxc send` reclaims an
expired lease too — that is how whoever is already in line gets the copy before whoever happens to
ask — and it had every one of the sweep's conditions except the park, so a dead operation's work was
still handed on in the tree whenever a trigger got there before a tick did. It parks first now, under
the same occasion and the same refusal rule: if the park is refused for a reason that can pass,
**nobody** takes the copy — the newcomer queues behind the holder exactly as it would have while the
lease was live, and the service's retry is what eventually moves it. That holds **even when nobody
else is waiting at all**, which is the most ordinary shape of it: one agent working alone crashes
with uncommitted work, the bound passes, and the next `nxc send` is the hand-off. There is no turn to
hand out then, but the copy still leaves an operation that came to grief, so its work goes onto a
branch first and the newcomer starts in a clean tree. The background sweep does not cover that one
and is not meant to: with an empty queue it hands nothing on, so there is nothing there to save. Neither park finding makes a
verb exit non-zero: `work_not_parked` and `work_handed_on_unparked` are reports on the receipt and in
`--json`, and a routine reclaim in a workspace that is not a git repository (where no park can ever
succeed) no longer fails the call it happened during.

**Facade contract.** `TriggerAdmission::Queued`'s `drain_unarmed: Option<FailedConsequence>` becomes
`findings: Vec<FailedConsequence>` — one list, because that hand-off can now report a park beside the
un-armed drain; a caller that built or destructured the variant has to name the new field, and
`TriggerReceipt::warnings` carries the same values it always did.
`WorkingTreeSweep` (on `TickReceipt::working_tree`) gains two public fields,
`parked: Option<Parked>` and `unparked: Option<ParkRefusal>`, so a struct literal outside the crate
has to name them; both are omitted from `--json` when unset. `ParkOccasion` gains the variant
`PastItsBound` (`past_its_bound` in `--json` and on `StatusOperation::park_refused.occasion`); the
enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so an exhaustive `match` outside the crate already had a wildcard.

### Removed
- **`nxc release` and `Engine::release_working_tree` are gone.** The verb gave a workspace's held
working copy back by hand, on the strength of one refusal: it checked that no session in the holding
chain still had a live process. Offered on the agent surface, that made it able to take a working
copy away from a running coding operation, and on a chat worker that never implemented the liveness
check it was an unconditional release with no guard at all — exactly the blunt override this
project's own epic on manual overrides declined to build, reached anyway because the refusal was the
only thing standing between the verb and it.

Every hand-off now PARKS the holder's work first, so what the verb used to do by hand happens on its
own. A working copy held by a chain that has died is parked and handed on by the background service
without anyone asking — past its two-hour bound, or, since the background service can now tell a
dead chain from a merely quiet one, inside it. A working copy held by a chain that is still running,
and that you — the person who started it — want back on purpose, is taken with `nxc withdraw
--thread <id>` / `Engine::withdraw`:
it discharges the round, asks its session to stop, and parks whatever it left uncommitted once the
process is gone — never rolled back — so the next commission into the same thread brings the work
back.

**Facade contract.** `Engine::release_working_tree` and `orchestration::release_working_tree` are
removed, along with `ReleaseReceipt`. `ChatStore::release_working_tree_and_take_next` is unaffected
and stays: it is the transaction every hand-off — the reply path, a park, the sweep — still goes
through to give the lease back and hand it to whoever is next.
